Mallards (*Anas platyrhynchos*) are among the most widespread and recognizable waterfowl species across the Northern Hemisphere. Commonly encountered in urban parks, rural ponds, and natural wetlands, they are known for their dietary adaptability and resilience. While frequently perceived as sedentary park birds, wild mallards display diverse and flexible movement strategies in response to local resource availability and seasonal changes.

This study focuses on wild mallards tagged at Lake Constance (Bodensee), a major freshwater lake situated at the junction of Germany, Switzerland, and Austria. The lake serves as a critical pre-Alpine crossroads and wintering site for migratory waterbirds traveling across European flyways.

High-resolution GPS tracking collars fitted to 52 individuals between 2007 and 2017 reveal striking individual variation in movement patterns. While some ducks remain near Lake Constance throughout the entire year, others undertake extensive seasonal migrations spanning hundreds of kilometers across Central Europe.
